newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says U.S. troops could guard Hebron settlers.
newsitem.headline: PLO says U.S. troops could guard Hebron settlers.

text.p: The PLO said on Tuesday it was ready to have U.S. troops guard Jewish settlers in the West Bank town of Hebron if that would calm Israeli security fears.

"We said we can ask for American forces to protect the settlers but we will not accept changing the agreement or Israeli intervention in areas under Palestinian jurisdiction," Nabil Abu Rdainah, an aide to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, told Reuters.
Israeli negotiating team spokesman Moshe Fogel said in reaction: "We do not want to go into the details of the various proposals."

An Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron should have been carried out in March but was delayed by Israel's previous centre-left government after Islamic suicide bombers killed 59 people in Israel in February and March.
The deal was frozen by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who says it must be changed to ensure the security of 400 Jewish settlers living in enclaves amid 100,000 Arabs in Hebron.
The Palestine Liberation Organisation refuses to amend the Hebron accord it signed with the former government, ousted in May elections.
U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross is mediating negotiations that began last week between Israel and the Palestinians on implementing the deal.
The negotiations were decided on at an emergency Washington summit after fierce clashes last month in which 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed.
